seeds.why: fallback: keep the cut, author fresh good phrases
seeds.fellBackBecause: Opus rejected: 'to put' = 'mettere' is already a sound, flexible LEGO: a real unit of intention, an infinitive that combines with many verbs. Its lack of USE phrases most likely comes from limited taught vocabulary at seed 53, not from a bad cut. The rule says not to change a LEGO that is already sound, so the right action is a topup with fresh phrases. Phrases like 'she wanted to put his letter in her bag' build from taught LEGOs alone. The merge also deletes L1 'she wanted to' = 'voleva', which already has 8 good USE phrases. That changes something that was fine and leaves a learner-useful unit as a hidden component. Chunking up is only justified when the short LEGO cannot be practised, and that is not shown here.

seeds.why: 'ti dispiace se ti faccio' is a sound, flexible unit that a learner would want to say, and merging it with 'domande' would exceed 8 syllables, so I keep the cut and write fresh phrases, including USE ones that pair it with the already taught 'domande'.
